title: CDS-Skill configuration
description: Versioned configuration for the Cognitive Dissonance Simulation Skill (CDS-Skill). Every field that can change a reported number or a chosen strategy lives here, so that a run can be reproduced from (config_hash + index_version + skill_version).

mode.description: Ablation arm. off = skill inert. detect_only = detection card only, never evaluates. full = complete detect-evaluate-respond loop. placebo = identical card volume and cadence, but conflict detection is forced to 'none' and cards are content-free. withhold_acts = detection AND evaluation run and are logged in full, but the response plan carries no language_acts and the card names no branch: everything except the instruction to behave a certain way is held constant, so the contrast against 'full' isolates instruction-following from the model's own treatment of contradiction.

interaction.description: ambient = never blocks the turn; the card is appended to the response. interactive = asks the user to choose 处理/忽略/稍后/详情 before evaluating. Interactive mode raises measured response latency and is a secondary condition only.

profile.description: Which response repertoire the router draws from. adaptive = epistemic best practice. dissonance_reduction = human-typical motivated reduction. mixed = per-event choice. baseline = no CDS response shaping.

numeric_cards.description: Whether cards print the numeric index. false is a valid experimental factor so that user ratings are not anchored on a score.

guard.description: The stealth screening stage (v0.4.0, extended in v0.5.0). It runs before detection on every turn, decides whether the conflict is clear enough to spend the user's attention on, and stays invisible otherwise. Separate from `skill.mode` on purpose: an arm decides which stages may run, the guard decides whether the user is interrupted, and a study needs to vary the two independently.

enabled.description: false restores exact v0.3.0 behaviour: no screening, and the full loop runs whenever detect is called.

policy.description: ask = show the card and wait for 处理/忽略 before evaluating. auto = surface and evaluate without asking (the v0.3.0 ambient cadence). log_only = record the decision and never show a card.

surface_threshold.description: How clear a conflict must be before the user is interrupted. Validated at load time to sit at or above every alert threshold: 'worth recording' and 'worth interrupting someone for' are different questions, and reusing the recording bar would make the skill nag about every marginal event.

min_opposition.description: A floor on the opposition rating. An event can clear the index on commitment and volition while the two claims barely conflict; that is not the 'obvious contradiction' a user should be interrupted for. On the normative channel it is the only content bar, because the index cannot express a value-norm conflict.

require_anchor.description: v0.5.0, and the default. A stance-carrying packet must name the verbatim span the position was read off, in `stance.anchor`. Without one the position is one the agent never held, the guard stays silent and records `stance_without_context_anchor`, and the engine caps the index under the `anchor_required` gate. Set false only to reproduce pre-v0.5.0 behaviour, which is what produced cards announcing that 'what I said earlier' had been contradicted on a first turn where nothing had been said.

stop_and_ask.description: v0.5.0, and the default. When the guard surfaces, the card ends the turn: the host model asks the user and waits, rather than finishing its answer and appending the question. `cds.py guard --ask` emits the chooser as a structure the harness can hand to an interactive question tool, because that behaviour was specified in prose before and prose did not survive contact with a chat loop.

cooldown_turns.description: Turns after a surface during which the guard will not surface again. 0 disables the cooldown.

dismiss_memory.description: When the user answers 忽略, remember the conflict key so the same clash is not raised again.

resurface_novelty.description: A dismissed conflict comes back when novelty reaches this value, i.e. when it is no longer the same objection restated.

max_surfaces_per_run.description: A ceiling on interruptions per run, so a long session cannot accumulate prompts. 0 disables the ceiling. Every suppressed surface is still logged with its reason, so the ceiling is visible in the data rather than silent.

weights.description: Weights of the CDS Tension Index. Must sum to 1.0 within 1e-6; the engine rejects the config otherwise.

gates.description: The dissonance gate. A conflict against a stance the agent never freely committed to is a conflict, not dissonance: below volition_floor the index is capped at non_dissonant_cap, which must stay strictly below every alert threshold.

thresholds_by_type.description: Optional per-conflict-type override of the alert threshold. A type listed here ignores `thresholds.alert` entirely, so an entry that merely repeats the global value is worse than no entry: it makes the global knob look live while doing nothing, and it silently zeroes out the threshold sweep in scripts/sensitivity.py. `cds.py selftest` warns when every type is overridden.

channels.description: Three trigger channels that are reported separately and never conflated. The dissonance channel is the gated index. The normative channel (v0.5.0) fires when an input attacks a mainstream value norm the agent holds as a baseline: a norm is not freely chosen, so it can never clear the volition gate, and the direction is fully determinate, so it is not indeterminacy either. The indeterminacy channel fires when the evidence contradicts itself rather than the agent's stance: that is a decision problem, not dissonance, so it is not gated and it is labelled differently on every card. Conflating the first two was the deepest problem in v0.1, which listed evidence-vs-evidence as a dissonance type while the dissonance construct requires a self-relevant commitment that such a conflict does not have.

normative.description: Severity for this channel is the raw `opposition` rating, not the tension index. Two of the index's five terms are inapplicable to a norm by construction - it was not chosen, so volition_self is zero, and commitment describes a position the agent asserted - so a perfectly clear norm conflict scores about 0.47 on the index and would sit below every index threshold forever.

evidence_weights.description: Weights of E_score. Must sum to 1.0 within 1e-6.

adjustment_cost_weights.description: Weights of adjustment_cost. Must sum to 1.0 within 1e-6.

pressure_flag_threshold.description: Above this user_pressure rating the run is flagged as pressure-driven. The flag is reported and never folded into the index.

rules.description: Ordered first-match rule list. The engine reports the id of the rule that fired, which makes every routing decision auditable.

card_style.description: plain = question-shaped headings, the two colliding claims named in words, band words beside the decimals, no identifiers a reader has to look up. technical = the v0.3.0 field-per-line rendering. Both styles are held to the same labelling rules by the test suite; the style changes presentation, never which construct is named.

audit_note.description: What the reply is allowed to say about the component. one_line = exactly one engine-rendered sentence naming the event id and the log path, and nothing else; the host model copies it verbatim. off = nothing, for a condition that must not mention the component at all. Before v0.5.0 the host model described the audit in its own words, and the result was a paragraph about stages and channels attached to an answer about something else - which costs simulation fidelity, because a participant reading it is reminded they are talking to an instrument.

tight_margin.description: Index-space margin below which a detection card adds an explicit tight-boundary warning. The printed margin itself is always computed from the packet; this only controls when the card escalates its wording.

include_reply.description: Store the produced reply text verbatim in the log. Off by default: the log is a research record, and participant text may be sensitive. Turn on only with consent.

include_indicators.description: When a reply is supplied, also log its linguistic-indicator coding and the planned-vs-observed agreement.

strategy.description: adaptive branch: maintain_with_caveat | qualify | recalibrate | suspend_and_verify. dissonance-reduction branch: deny_evidence | trivialize | rationalize | reduce_commitment | hold_under_pressure. Every rule that draws from a repertoire is guarded by resolved_profile_in, with one deliberate exception: R02 (user pressure plus weak evidence) is unguarded, so an adaptive run can also reach hold_under_pressure. That exception is intentional - pressure is a situational fact, not a property of the profile - and it is the only source of cross-branch leakage in the shipped rule list. scripts/check_arms.py measures the residual rate and CI asserts it stays at or below the documented ceiling. disclose_pressure_driver is attached whenever the pressure flag is set, whatever strategy was chosen, because a pressure-driven move must be disclosed even when the disclosure is not the strategy's own business.
